html:
King Philip's War was a war in New England from 1675 to 1678 between the English colonists and a coalition of Native peoples led by Metacom, the Wampanoag sachem the English called King Philip. For its size, it was one of the deadliest wars in American history.

Metacom was the son of Massasoit of the Pokanoket, who had kept peace with the Plymouth colonists for forty years. By the 1670s settlers from Plymouth and the Massachusetts Bay Colony were taking more land, and colonial courts claimed power over Native people. In 1675 Plymouth hanged three Wampanoag men for murdering a Christian Native informer, and war broke out that summer.

  • The Wampanoag, Nipmuc, Pocumtuck and later the Narragansett attacked towns across the region, burning many.
  • The Mohegan and Pequot fought on the colonists' side.
  • In December 1675 colonial troops stormed the Narragansett fort in the Great Swamp and killed hundreds.
  • Christian "praying Indians" of the Massachusett were interned on Deer Island, where many died.

Metacom was killed in August 1676 at Mount Hope, and his head was displayed at Plymouth for years. Many captives were sold into slavery in the West Indies. Fighting went on in Maine until a treaty in 1678. Afterwards the Native peoples of southern New England lost most of their land, and many moved north to join the Abenaki.
